title: Input Groups
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of input groups and when it is appropriate.
Apply text prefixes and suffixes using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check buttons inside input groups and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study input groups and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Input Groups should guide users through a form rather than merely decorate controls. Associate labels and help text with fields, preserve native semantics, and validate submitted data on the server as well as in the browser.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input groups as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
